editorialNarrative.hook: Rabada's absence and two South African spinners make Durban a test of Australia's batting adaptability, not simply its pace attack.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: Kingsmead begins a three-Test contest between the last two World Test Championship winners, before Gqeberha and Cape Town. South Africa's announced XI is confirmed; Australia's touring options are not a promised playing XI. Kayo and Fox Cricket carry the series in Australia. No first-Test result has been assumed.
editorialNarrative.formCopy: South Africa have named Maharaj and Harmer together, with Nortje returning alongside Jansen. Rabada remains unavailable for the opener. Australia's batting faces its own scrutiny after the drawn Bangladesh series; Labuschagne retained his place, while the touring squad includes Kuhnemann as a second specialist spin option.
editorialNarrative.closingCopy: This is Australia's first Test tour here since 2018. The legacy belongs to the series, but Durban's immediate argument is cricketing: can the visitors establish authority against a home attack built around more than fast bowling? For the Proteas, depth has to replace a missing spearhead.
